# WU-17 — Input and output limits (prompt-injection hardening): plan

**Status:** approved (2026-11-10) with every plan-review recommendation: P1 #1, #2 and P2 #3, #4, #6, #7 are folded into this plan; #5 is kept (CP2 gets an Opus checkpoint review). Q1: the D7 caps as listed. Q2: breaking, `0.3.0`; the contract stays in 0.x until it is complete (a WU-16 Note proposing the 1.0.0 declaration comes at the CP2 stop).

**Branch note.** Rebased onto `main` after #16 (`refactor(repo): move language-neutral spec files to spec/`) before CP0. Only paths changed: generated files, `rules.md` and fixtures now live under `spec/`.

**Review tier:** `opus` (§8). **Granularity:** `fine` (§9).

## 1. Goal & scope

**Goal** (from `docs/work-breakdown.md`): limit what prompt injection and API abuse can achieve. Every free-text value the API accepts or returns has a cap. Oversized input is rejected at the wire, and an injected instruction that gets past the model can yield only a few short strings, never free-form output paid for with our tokens.

**In scope**
- The length-counting spike (done while planning; result in D1) and ADR 0003.
- A cap on `ExtractResponse.clarificationQuestion`, the one free-form model output of `/extract` (plan review #1).
- Cap constants in `src/wire/constants.ts`, copied into `spec/generated/constants.json`.
- `.max()` on every string and array reachable from `TripProfile`, and on `ExtractRequest.message`. Every request that carries a profile (`ExtractRequest.currentProfile`, `RecommendRequest.profile`, `PresentRequest.profile`) and `ExtractResponse.profile` inherit the caps, because they all reuse `TripProfile`.
- `normalize` discards over-cap values and reports what it discarded.
- Language-neutral normalize fixtures, so later backends match.
- Conformance boundary checks (200 at the cap, 422 at the cap plus one) and their self-tests.
- CLAUDE.md §4.4, §4.5 and §4.7 updated; `contractVersion` bumped (D9).

**Out of scope**
- Strings in `Recommendation`, `RecommendationSet` and `PresentationModel` (WU-10, WU-11).
- Wiring `normalize` into `/extract`, logging discards, and `maxOutputTokens` sizing (WU-09).
- The web input's `maxlength` (WU-13).
- Changing `MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES` (R6).
- Everything in ADR 0003's Future hardening section (backlog, WU-18).
- Placeholder code for `api-fastapi` / `api-go` (CLAUDE.md §9).

## 2. Approach & key decisions

| # | Decision | Why / CLAUDE.md | Rejected alternative |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | **Length = Unicode code points.** Spike (pinned `zod 4.6.7`, Ajv 2020 defaults): Zod's `.max()` counts code points (`$ZodCheckMaxLength` falls back to `util.codePointLength` when the UTF-16 count is over), and Ajv's `maxLength` counts code points (`unicode: true` default). `'🌴'.repeat(3)` passes `max(3)` in both. Python `len(str)` and pydantic `max_length` count code points. Go must use `utf8.RuneCountInString`, not `len` (bytes). Lone surrogates are pinned for TS only (one code point in Zod and Ajv) and unspecified across backends, since pydantic may reject them outright (plan review #6); no conformance check sends one. Combining marks count separately everywhere (`é` = 2). | One definition every language can implement with its standard library, and it is what JSON Schema specifies, so the generated schemas mean the same thing everywhere (§4.1). | UTF-16 units (JS-only; would need Ajv `unicode: false`, unavailable in Python/Go validators). Bytes (penalizes non-Latin scripts; JSON Schema can't express it). Grapheme clusters (needs ICU-level tables; differs by Unicode version). |
| D2 | **Pin the counting with tests**, not trust: parity samples at exactly the cap and cap+1 in astral characters, plus a lone-surrogate sample, through `schemas.test.ts` and `parity.test.ts`. A Zod or Ajv upgrade that changes counting fails them. | §6.1/§6.5: portability is proven by tests. | A comment in the schema. |
| D3 | **Resource limits go on the wire (422); business rules stay off it.** Caps are `.max()` on `z.string()` / `z.array()` in `trip-profile.ts` and `envelopes.ts`. They are JSON-Schema-expressible (`maxLength` / `maxItems`), so other backends get them from `generated/`. | §4.1 allows constraints that JSON Schema expresses. §4.5's "no constraints on profile fields" exists so a `needs_clarification` response can carry a bad value back; a cap isn't a clarification, it's abuse protection, and D5 guarantees the server never returns an over-cap value. CLAUDE.md §4.5 gets an explicit exception. | A rule code (`TEXT_TOO_LONG`): returns 200 and puts the long value back into the next prompt, which is exactly what the cap is meant to stop. |
| D4 | **`ExtractionSchema` gets no caps** (ADR 0001 Q3). The model's output is unconstrained; `normalize` enforces the caps in code. The existing JSON keyword walk in `constructs.test.ts` already fails on `maxLength`/`maxItems` there, so this needs no new test. | A constraint the SDK validates turns one long value into a 502 for the whole call (§4.4). | Caps in `ExtractionSchema`. |
| D5 | **`normalize` discards, never truncates.** <br>• An over-cap optional string (`region`, `departure.city`, `people[i].gender`, `dateRange.note`) is dropped as if `null`; a parent left empty is dropped as before (`departure`, flexible `dateRange`). <br>• An over-cap fixed `start` or `end` drops the whole `dateRange` (both are required in the fixed variant). <br>• An over-cap `unmappedExperiences` item is dropped on its own. <br>• A list still over its count cap after item filtering (`experiences`, `unmappedExperiences`, `people`) is dropped whole. A list left empty is dropped as before. <br>• A value at exactly the cap is kept unchanged. | A truncated string can change meaning, and keeps the prefix of an injected payload. Dropping a value makes it "not mentioned", which the existing rules already handle (often `INSUFFICIENT_DETAIL` → clarification). A party list cut to its first N travelers would misstate the party; dropping it gets the user asked again. | Truncating strings. Keeping the first N list items. Failing the request with a 502 (lets an attacker turn any message into an error). |
| D6 | **`normalize` returns `{ profile, discarded }`.** `discarded` is `Discard[]`, `{ path, limit: 'maxLength' \| 'maxItems' }`, `path` a JSON Pointer into the extraction (`/people/3/gender`, `/unmappedExperiences/2`, `/dateRange/start`, `/people`), in document order. Reporting rules (plan review #3): every value that was over a cap is reported at its own path; a list dropped whole for its count is reported as the list alone (`/people`, `maxItems`), not the over-cap values inside it; a parent dropped because it became empty (`departure`, flexible `dateRange`) is not reported, since it was not over a cap; item paths use the extraction's original indices; the count check uses the length after over-cap items are removed. It is exported from `./rules` (backends only) and is **not** wire. | WU-09 logs it as a security signal (WU-09 Note). A return value keeps `normalize` pure (§6.1). The only callers today are tests. | A second `normalizeWithReport()` (two functions to keep in step). A logging callback (impure). |
| D7 | **Cap values** (code points / items), well above any honest value: <br>• `MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH = 2000` <br>• `MAX_SHORT_TEXT_LENGTH = 100`: `region`, `departure.city`, `gender`, each `unmappedExperiences` item <br>• `MAX_NOTE_LENGTH = 300`: `dateRange.note` <br>• `MAX_DATE_TEXT_LENGTH = 32`: fixed `start` / `end` (above 10, so a malformed-but-plausible date such as `2027-06-01T00:00:00Z` still reaches `DATE_VALID` and gets a clarification) <br>• `MAX_LIST_ITEMS = 20`: `experiences`, `unmappedExperiences` (the enum has 10 values) <br>• `MAX_TRAVELERS = 50`: `people` <br>• `MAX_CLARIFICATION_LENGTH = 500`: `ExtractResponse.clarificationQuestion`, a server guarantee that §4.5 already allows on a non-profile field; WU-09 treats an over-cap question as a model failure (retry once, then 502). Violation `params` strings stay uncapped: they echo profile values that are already capped. <br>`constants.json` gains `maxMessageLength`, `maxClarificationLength`, `maxShortTextLength`, `maxNoteLength`, `maxDateTextLength`, `maxListItems`, `maxTravelers`. Integers get no new caps: `z.int()` already bounds them to safe integers, and their ranges are rules. | Q1 asks the user to confirm the numbers. Flat camelCase keys match the existing `constants.json`. | One cap for all strings (either too loose for `region` or too tight for `note`). |
| D8 | **The normalize spec lives in `spec/rules.md`** as a new `## Normalization` section (with the code-point definition under `## Definitions`), and its cases in `spec/fixtures/normalize/*.json`: `{ id, ac, description, extraction, expectedProfile, expectedDiscarded }`. A test-only loader parses them through `ExtractionSchema` / `TripProfile` with the same deep-equal guard as `rule-fixtures.ts` (unknown keys fail). | `rules.md` is already the language-neutral spec every backend implements (ADR 0002); one file is easier to find than two. | A separate `normalize.md` (CLAUDE.md §2 layout doesn't list it). TS-only unit tests (later backends couldn't match). |
| D9 | **Breaking contract change**: requests that were valid can now get a 422. CP2 is `feat(domain-schema)!:` with a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer, and `CONTRACT_VERSION` goes `0.2.0` → `0.3.0`. No client exists yet (WU-12). | §4.3 / §10. | A minor bump: understates the change. |
| D10 | **"Always parses" is a deterministic combinatorial test**, not a property-based one: for every capped field, extractions at the cap, at cap+1 (ASCII and astral), and two with every field over its cap at once (one with a fixed `dateRange`, one flexible); `TripProfile.safeParse(normalize(x).profile)` must succeed for each, and `discarded` must list exactly the over-cap paths. | Covers every cap edge with no new dependency and no randomness (§6.1). | Adding `fast-check` with a fixed seed (a new dep for cases we can enumerate). |
| D11 | **Conformance boundaries** (`tests/contract/conformance/checks/limits.ts`), caps read from `constants.json`: <br>• `/extract`: `message` of exactly `maxMessageLength` astral code points → 200 (catches a backend counting UTF-16 units or bytes); cap+1 → 422 `VALIDATION_FAILED`, in ASCII and in astral. <br>• `/extract`: `currentProfile.region` at `maxShortTextLength` → 200; cap+1 → 422. <br>• `/recommend` and `/present`: `profile.region` at cap+1 → 422. <br>The 200 checks stay on `/extract` only, so only WU-09 has to record cassettes for them (Note). Self-tests: the fake backend (Ajv-validating, so it enforces the caps once regenerated) passes; a hook that accepts over-cap bodies fails; a hook that counts UTF-16 units fails the at-cap check. | §6.5: black-box, reads only `generated/`. 422 needs no LLM call, so testing it on every endpoint is free. | 200-at-cap on every endpoint (WU-10/11 would need cassettes for odd requests). |
| D12 | **`api-nextjs` needs no code change.** `postRoute` parses with the Zod request schemas, so the caps apply, and `jsonResponse` refuses (500) to send an over-cap profile. The conformance run against `api-nextjs` proves it. | §9: thin adapters. | An extra route integration test (duplicates conformance). |

## 6. Risks & open questions

- **Q1 — cap values.** Decided: D7 as listed.
- **Q2 — breaking bump.** Decided: breaking, `0.3.0`.
- **R1 — Zod's counting is version behavior.** Older Zod counted UTF-16 units. D2's astral samples catch a change on upgrade.
- **R2 — Python and Go are not installed here.** D1's Python/Go findings come from their documentation, not a run. They are proven when those backends run the conformance suite (D11's astral at-cap check fails a Go backend that uses `len`).
- **R3 — `normalize`'s signature changes** (D6). No production caller yet; WU-09 is the first. Recorded as a Note on WU-09.
- **R4 — cassette burden.** After WU-09 replaces the `/extract` stub, D11's two 200-at-cap requests need cassettes. Proposed Note on WU-09.
- **R5 — rule parity for normalize.** ADR 0002's results check covers `spec/fixtures/rules` only. Proposed Note on WU-09: run `spec/fixtures/normalize` through `/extract` with the mock client too, and extend the results check to their ids.
- **R6 — `MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES` stays 1 MiB.** `PresentRequest.recommendations` is uncapped until WU-10/11, so the body cap can't shrink yet. Proposed Note on WU-11: revisit it once every string is capped.

## 8. Unit review tier

**`opus`**: the unit changes the contract (CLAUDE.md §12 4a, and the WU-17 Note), and `normalize`'s discard semantics become every backend's behavior.

## 9. Granularity

**`fine`**: a breaking contract change plus a new cross-language spec; small, separately reviewable slices keep the Opus review focused on CP2.
